summary:
Once, this delicate cactus clung to the branches of trees along the coastal hills of Rio de Janeiro and Niterói, thriving in the humid air rising from Guanabara Bay. A member of the remarkable mistletoe cactus family, it grew as an epiphyte — rootless in soil, instead weaving itself into the forest canopy at elevations up to 600 meters.

As Rio expanded, its forests disappeared beneath concrete, and this species was swallowed by the city it now barely haunts. Today, a handful of plants survive on trees in public parks — refugees in an urban landscape growing hotter and drier each year. It may already be extinct in any true wild sense, its story a quiet warning written in vanishing green.
